newsitem.title: JAPAN: NORDIC SKIING-TOUGH OLYMPIC COURSE EARNS PRAISE.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-TOUGH OLYMPIC COURSE EARNS PRAISE.

text.p: The tough hilly course where Italians swept four World Cup cross-country ski races at the weekend earned widespread praise from Olympic-bound competitors.
But some coaches criticised the logistics of getting to the venue.

Italian head coach Alessandro Vanoi, who brought an 18-member staff to test equipment and snow conditions in preparation for next year's Olympic races to be held on the same course, said the commute from the athletes village in Nagano was too long.
"I can't understand why the organising committee doesn't organise a village here in Hakuba," said Vanoi.
The Italians have already arranged hotel rooms for their skiers in Hakuba during the Olympics to spare them the daily drive from Nagano.
The 37-km (23-mile) commute on a single-lane highway, which has been upgraded for the Games, takes about an hour even without the heavy traffic burden expected during the Olympics.
Coaches also asked organisers to hold Olympic events earlier in the day, when snow conditions are more predictable. Women's races started at 10:15 a.m. on the weekend and men's races at noon.
Silvio Fauner won the mens 15-km pursuit event on Sunday after taking the 10-km classic race on Saturday.
Teammate Giorgio Di Centa outsprinted Jari Isometsa of Finland to place second in the pursuit.
Norwegian Bjorn Dahling retained his lead in the men's World Cup standings despite finishing fifth in the pursuit and sixth in the classic event.

Stefania Belmondo's win on Sunday in the womens 10-km pursuit race vaulted her into first place in the women's standings ahead of Elena Vaelbe of Russia. Belmondo also won the womens five-km classic on Saturday.
Katerina Neumannova of the Czech Republic finished second on Sunday while Vaelbe was third.
